summary: 1939 Huxford fire tower moved to private land near Georgiana after 2006 AFC surplus; the Spring Hill former site keeps only its stands.

facts.design: 100-foot International Derrick model Huxford fire tower with 7 by 7 foot cab
facts.status_note: Standing at Georgiana after relocation; the Spring Hill former site retains only its stands.

access.note: On the owner's property near Georgiana; the register gives no public visiting arrangement.

events.note: NHLR gives 1939 as the build year for the Huxford tower
Declared surplus by the Alabama Forestry Commission in 2006; Jerry Watson then purchased, moved and restored it
Former-sites record for the Spring Hill Longleaf Fire Tower Site, registered September 15, 2019

evidence.supports: design: 100-foot International Derrick model Huxford tower with 7 by 7 foot cab, built 1939
evidence.quote: When the 100' International Derrick model Huxford fire tower with 7'x7' cab (1939) was declared surplus by AFC in 2006, Jerry Watson purchased, moved and carefully restored the structure as his own Longleaf Lookout Tower.

evidence.supports: Watson's land is a longleaf pine property the register calls Georgiana; tower stands in Butler County
evidence.quote: It now stands in Butler as a historic complement to his own longleaf pine forest known as Georgiana.

evidence.supports: register elevation 323 ft (98 m) for the moved tower
Spring Hill location; only stands remain at the former site
evidence.quote: Located in forested area in Spring Hill next to church. Follow former service road to site. Stands are all that remain.

evidence.supports: former site administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR places the moved tower at Georgiana in Butler County (31.649477, -86.890528). The former-sites register lists a Longleaf Fire Tower Site in Spring Hill about 0.7 km east (31.65, -86.8835), where only the stands remain. The two records do not say the Spring Hill site is where the tower originally stood; treated as an inference from the shared name.
Register elevations differ (323 ft for the moved tower, 297 ft for the Spring Hill site). Consistent with two different locations; not a conflict about one tower.

notes_for_editor: The 2006 surplus, the purchase, the move and the restoration rest on the NHLR entry alone. A private commercial page about the tower appeared in search (longleafcamp.com) but could not be reached from this environment (DNS failure), and search snippets from it and other results mention a 1985 closure and a 110 ft height. Those claims are unverified and not used; the height in facts is the register's 100 ft. The NHLR 'Administered by' field names the owner, not an agency, so facts.agency records the owner. The Spring Hill link is inferred, not stated. Visiting status and current condition are undocumented. Photos: FFLOS credits Andrew Zerbe and NHLR credits a photo to a named contributor, but no image URLs were captured, so no photo entries were added.
